pr_title: tests: drivers: gpio: skip unsupported tests
pr_body:
Some drivers may not support simultaneous input-output configuration or disconnect.

In such cases, the driver should return `-ENOTSUP` and the test should be skipped.

Fixes #46917

* Also update the suite to use the new ztest API
* Also correct error codes for related functions in `gpio.h`
pr_comments: I tried this PR but the failure is still the same on nrf boards

> I tried this PR but the failure is still the same on nrf boards

@PerMac 
nRF boards do not yet support get direction, so that is expected.

Would be great if Nordic could add that support.
Probably worth it to skip tests if the driver does not support getting direction.
I see, but then it means the test description in its yaml requires some extra filtering options, so boards without getting direction won't be picked up

@PerMac - skipping test at runtime for now :P I think proper filtering would likely require adding a Kconfig until there is support everywhere (e.g. `CONFIG_GPIO_DRIVER_SUPPORTS_DIRECTION`) but that seems like it could be overkill.
@yperess - need to re-approve due to force-push, sorry.

TBH I am ambivalent about this solution. We will spend resources on our testing farm for building and executing a test, which in the end results only in skips. I can also imagine, that there is no other reasonable way for filtration in this case. However, if you'd managed to find a filtration option I'd appreciate it :)

Had we included this test in the basic GPIO API test, and just skipped it for drivers not implementing this feature, the overhead would have been smaller.

> > @PerMac - Ideally @anangl would be able to add support for `gpio_get_direction()` along with the fix for #47030, and then the test would be useful on nRF as well.
> 
> Had we included this test in the basic GPIO API test, and just skipped it for drivers not implementing this feature, the overhead would have been smaller.

If (when?) all platforms implement `gpio_get_direction()`, then I think it would make sense to merge it into the basic api test, because at that point, it would be part of the basic api and not `[EXPERIMENTAL]`.

issue_context.title: frdm_k64f : failed to run tests/drivers/gpio/gpio_get_direction
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Two bugs here , in test_disconnect and test_input_output function , shows "gpio_pin_configure() failed: -134".
It seems that these two flags are not recognized: "GPIO_INPUT | GPIO_OUTPUT | GPIO_OUTPUT_INIT_LOW"  , "GPIO_DISCONNECTED" .

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. source zephyr-env.sh
2. twister -p frdm_k64f --device-testing  --hardware-map map.yml -T tests/drivers/gpio/gpio_get_direction/ -vv
3. See error

or

2. west build -p always -b frdm_k64f tests/drivers/gpio/gpio_get_direction/
3. screen /dev/ttyACM0 115200
4. west flash
5. See error

**Expected behavior**
Test case should pass as expected.

**Impact**
The testsuite gpio_get_direction failed.

**Logs and console output**
```
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v3.1.0-812-g88ca3aca98c0  ***
Running TESTSUITE gpio_get_direction
===================================================================
START - test_disconnect
Assertion failed at WEST_TOPDIR/zephyr/tests/drivers/gpio/gpio_get_direction/src/main.c:20: test_disconnect: (0 not equal to rv)
gpio_pin_configure() failed: -134
FAIL - test_disconnect in 0.15 seconds

TESTSUITE gpio_get_direction failed.
===================================================================
RunID: c8e7e0ad19f305178da49e64f6b23b25

```
**Environment :**
OS: Linux
Toolchain Zephyr SDK 0.14.1
Commit SHA or Version: 88ca3aca98c0788e2c45db5c3fb9c8523293a8c0

Ack- copy-paste error. It went into the wrong function. Will fix

Actually, @PerMac it seems that `gpio_nrfx.c` (at least the driver, not sure about the hardware) does not support setting gpio disconnect (at least). Do you know whether it supports setting simultaneous input-output?

It seems rather than reporting `-ENOTSUP`, the `gpio_nrfx.c` driver returns `-EIO`, which is likely a driver bug.
```
 * @retval 0 If successful.
 * @retval -ENOTSUP if any of the configuration options is not supported
 *                  (unless otherwise directed by flag documentation).
 * @retval -EINVAL Invalid argument.
 * @retval -EIO I/O error when accessing an external GPIO chip.
 * @retval -EWOULDBLOCK if operation would block.
 */
__syscall int gpio_pin_configure(const struct device *port,
```

See https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/include/zephyr/drivers/gpio.h#L681
@anangl can you please chip in? It is beyond my scope :(

> Actually, @PerMac it seems that `gpio_nrfx.c` (at least the driver, not sure about the hardware) does not support setting gpio disconnect (at least). Do you know whether it supports setting simultaneous input-output?

@cfriedt The gpio_nrfx driver supports simultaneous input-output pin configuration. It also supports the `GPIO_DISCONNECTED` flag, not perfectly though, as it incorrectly returns the `-EIO` error if the pin to be configured with `GPIO_DISCONNECTED` was not earlier configured as input or output. I can provide a fix for that - you can assign #47030 to me, unless you prefer to solve it yourself.
